stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.

Vasseur's job has come under increasing scrutiny over the past month, with reports last week linking ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner to replace him.

The speculation grew so much Ferrari felt the need this week to clarify that Ferrari's corporate leadership has "full confidence" in Vasseur, albeit via a press conference with the team's head of communications and not through a statement from either company CEO Benedetto Vigna or chairman John Elkann.

"Ultimately, it's not a one-man operation," Hamilton said in a passionate defence of his team boss to TV in Malaysia on Thursday. "If you want to point fingers, point them somewhere else. There are lot of people above that also are a part of it.

"So if you want to take something from this message: Fred's in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him. And I still believe fully in where we're going."

Speaking to the written media afterwards, Hamilton reiterated: "I think Fred has the full backing.

"There often seems to be a lot of focus on one individual in one role here. And you can see that, obviously, they've switched out lots of different people in Fred's role. But Fred is a fantastic leader.

"He really is the guy to take his team in the right direction. However, there is a structure that's been there for some time. Whether or not that needs looking at moving forward, there are obviously also people above Fred, and it's not about one person.

"Fred has led the team to ... He's helped make changes in this past year, he's helped us get to the second in the constructors' championship. That's a huge step from last year."

Hamilton was then asked if one of the issues Ferrari has is that Vasseur has no financial stake in the race team, unlike his former boss Toto Wolff, who oversees all facets of the Mercedes F1 team.

In reply to whether Ferrari could benefit with a similar structure to Mercedes, Hamilton said: "There are changes that I would make, but I'm not going to talk about what those are. Toto's in a different position to Fred. The structure's a lot different. That's all I can say."

Ferrari has always been subjected to intense scrutiny, attention which has likely only increased the longer the team's title drought has gone on -- the team's last constructors' title was 2008, with its last drivers' title in 2007.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Hamilton said the recent reporting about the state of the internals of the team have been wide of the market.

"For me, it's frustrating to see all the negativity. Because you see other people making mistakes, and they don't normally say too much about them," he said.

"We either make the same mistake, or are not perfect and and it's ten times worse for some reason for Ferrari, but that's also to be expected. Given that it's the best brand here, it's the most iconic by far. For me, I don't read a lot, so that has zero effect on me. But of course, when I come into the room and see, it definitely affects individuals on the team.

"Because every weekend they try and show up and do the best job they can, and they don't get it right all the time. Families are messaging you for all the negative things that they're reading when the people back at the factory are reading all those things, even though they're giving their all. It's almost like sometimes you feel like there's nothing you can do right, even when you're giving your all.

"For me, the message is to not read any of the stuff that's being written. Because the fact is, nobody that's writing any of the stuff has actually any clue what they're talking about, because they're not in the team.

"They don't know what's happening behind closed doors. They don't know how hard everybody's working. It's all down to assumptions and opinions."

Vasseur and Hamilton worked together back in Formula 2 before being reunited at Ferrari.

"Fred's been fantastic working with me and I think our relationship as a whole -- even with our bosses -- is in a better place than it ever was," he added to television.

"Fred's made a lot of changes I've asked for already. I think it's not an easy time for Fred so I think it's good that the team came out with that earlier this week. I've also let him know I support him 100%.

"I wouldn't be here without Fred. Swapping him out ... it won't change how the team moves forwards. It would be detrimental to it."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 1

Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.
